::: {#exm-chronic-eda}
#### Exploring the chronic medical conditions data

@dobson4e [§2.2.1, Table 2.1] reports the number of chronic medical conditions
for 26 women living in a town
and 23 women living in the country,
all attending general practitioners.
We will carry this dataset through all four steps of the model fitting process.

| Symbol | Meaning | Column in `dobson::chronic` |
|--------|---------|---------------------|
| $Y_i$ | number of chronic medical conditions reported by woman $i$ | `number` (copied to `conditions`) |
| $x_i$ | indicator that woman $i$ lives in the country ($1$) rather than the town ($0$) | derived from `place` (stored as `country`) |

```{r}
#| label: chronic-data
data(chronic, package = "dobson")
chronic$conditions <- chronic$number
chronic$country <- as.numeric(chronic$place == "country")
chronic$residence <- chronic$place
```

Following the three questions of @dobson4e [§2.3.1]:

1. The outcome $Y$ is a count,
   so its scale of measurement is discrete and non-negative;
   the predictor $x$ is a [binary](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/data.html#def-binary-var) ([nominal](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/data.html#def-nominal-var)) [indicator](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/data.html#def-indicator-variable).

2. @tbl-chronic-counts shows the frequency distribution of $Y$ within each group.
   Both distributions are right-skewed,
   with most women reporting zero, one, or two conditions.

3. The town women report more conditions on average
   ([sample mean](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/exploratory-descriptive.html#def-sample-mean) `r round(mean(chronic$conditions[chronic$country == 0]), 3)`)
   than the country women
   (sample mean `r round(mean(chronic$conditions[chronic$country == 1]), 3)`),
   so residence might be associated with the outcome.

::: {#tbl-chronic-counts}

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
table(
  residence = chronic$residence,
  conditions = chronic$conditions
)
```

Frequency distribution of the number of chronic medical conditions,
by residence
[@dobson4e, §2.2.1, Table 2.1]
